item.content:encoded:
The COMSTECH Research Fellowships for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) in OIC provide an important opportunity for young scientists, engineers, and researchers from eligible Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) least developed countries to undertake advanced research and training at prestigious research and higher-education institutions across OIC member states.

The fellowship is offered by COMSTECH, in collaboration with member institutions of the COMSTECH Consortium of Excellence (CCoE). It is designed to strengthen research and development capacity among promising researchers, particularly those who are at the beginning of their research careers and those working in OIC least developed countries.

Successful fellows can spend 6 to 12 months at a relevant center of excellence, where they can undertake research, receive advanced training, work with experienced researchers, and develop professional links that may lead to future international research collaboration.

Unlike many scholarship and fellowship programs that operate according to a single annual deadline, this COMSTECH opportunity states that applications and nominations are open throughout the year.

About the COMSTECH Research Fellowship

The COMSTECH Research Fellowship program is intended to support scientific research and advanced training among researchers from eligible least developed OIC countries.

The fellowship allows successful applicants to spend an extended period at a relevant host institution within the OIC network. Depending on the research area and host institution, the placement can last between six and twelve months.

The program is particularly focused on researchers in:

  • Natural sciences
  • Applied sciences
  • Engineering
  • Technology

Through the fellowship, researchers have an opportunity to work within established research environments and develop their technical and scientific capabilities.

The program also seeks to encourage stronger research connections between institutions and researchers across OIC member states.

What Is the Purpose of the COMSTECH Fellowship?

The central purpose of the fellowship is to strengthen the research and development capacity of promising scientists and engineers.

COMSTECH recognizes the importance of supporting researchers early in their careers, particularly those who may have fewer opportunities to access advanced research facilities, specialist expertise, and international scientific networks.

The fellowship therefore seeks to provide researchers with opportunities to:

  1. Undertake research at established centers of excellence.
  2. Receive advanced scientific and technical training.
  3. Work with experienced researchers and mentors.
  4. Strengthen their research skills and professional expertise.
  5. Develop relationships with researchers and institutions in other OIC countries.
  6. Establish foundations for future research collaboration.
  7. Contribute to scientific and technological development in their home countries.

The program places particular emphasis on young scientists, with preference indicated for researchers who are at the beginning of their research careers.

Fellowship Duration

The COMSTECH research fellowship is offered for a period of:

6 to 12 months

The fellowship may be extended upon the recommendation of the host institution.

This relatively long placement allows researchers to become integrated into their host research environment rather than participating only in a short training program.

Depending on the research project and host institution, fellows may use the period to conduct experiments, undertake advanced research, receive specialized training, work alongside research teams, or develop new research collaborations.

Fields of Study and Research

The fellowship is specifically focused on scientific and technological disciplines.

Eligible fields include:

  • Natural Sciences
  • Applied Sciences
  • Engineering
  • Technology

Applicants should therefore have an academic and research background relevant to the proposed area of study or research.

The proposed research should also be suitable for the facilities, expertise, and research capacity available at the selected host institution.

Host Institutions

The fellowship is hosted by various research and higher-education institutions in OIC member states.

COMSTECH works with institutions that are part of its Consortium of Excellence (CCoE).

These institutions serve as research environments where selected fellows can undertake their projects and receive supervision and training.

Applicants are encouraged to identify a host institution that has relevant expertise and research facilities aligned with their proposed area of research.

The list of CCoE member institutions is provided by COMSTECH as part of the fellowship information.

Financial Support Provided

The fellowship includes support from both COMSTECH and the host institution.

International airfare

COMSTECH will bear the cost of international low-cost airfare for successful fellows.

This support helps eligible researchers travel from their home country to the country hosting their fellowship.

Accommodation and subsistence

The host institution is expected to provide:

  • Accommodation
  • Subsistence
  • Supervision
  • Local training and mentoring

This means the financial and logistical structure of the fellowship involves cooperation between COMSTECH and the participating host institution.

Research supervision and mentoring

Fellows are expected to benefit from supervision and mentoring at their host institutions.

This component is particularly valuable for early-career researchers who want to strengthen their research methodologies, technical capabilities, and professional networks.

Who Is the Fellowship Intended For?

The program is aimed at young scientists and engineers from least developed countries that are members of the OIC, as well as eligible researchers employed by research institutions in OIC countries.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to applicants who are:

  • Early-career researchers
  • Scientists
  • Engineers
  • Researchers undertaking active research
  • Professionals seeking advanced research training
  • Researchers holding at least an M.S. or equivalent qualification
  • Researchers holding a Ph.D. for post-graduate research
  • Researchers from OIC least developed countries
  • Researchers working in research institutions within OIC countries

Preference is given to young scientists, particularly women scientists, who are at the beginning of their research careers and those working in least developed OIC countries.

Minimum Academic Qualification

Applicants must meet the minimum academic requirements associated with the level of research or training they are pursuing.

For graduate studies

Applicants should hold at least an:

M.S. or equivalent degree

For post-graduate studies

Applicants should hold a:

Ph.D.

The program also indicates that applicants may be scientists or engineers involved in active research.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic qualifications and current research activities are clearly documented in their application.

Age Limit

The fellowship has age limits depending on the level of study.

Graduate studies

The maximum age is:

35 years

Post-graduate studies

The maximum age is:

45 years

Applicants should therefore carefully determine which category their proposed research or advanced training falls under before submitting their application.

Nationality and Geographic Eligibility

The fellowship is specifically intended for applicants connected to least developed countries of the OIC.

Eligible applicants include young scientists and engineers who are citizens of an OIC least developed country or who are employed by a research institution in an OIC country, subject to the program’s eligibility requirements.

The opportunity is therefore not a general worldwide fellowship open to applicants from every country.

Applicants should verify that their nationality or institutional affiliation meets COMSTECH’s current definition and list of eligible least developed OIC countries before applying.

Preference for Early-Career Researchers

One of the distinguishing features of the fellowship is its emphasis on researchers at the beginning of their research careers.

The program indicates that preference is given to:

  • Young scientists
  • Researchers beginning their scientific careers
  • Women scientists
  • Researchers working in least developed OIC countries

This emphasis means that applicants should clearly demonstrate how the fellowship would contribute to their development as researchers and how the experience could strengthen their future scientific work.

Selection Based on Scientific Merit

Fellowships are awarded based on scientific merit.

Applications are jointly reviewed by an expert committee involving COMSTECH and the relevant host institutions.

This makes the quality and relevance of the proposed research particularly important.

Applicants should therefore pay careful attention to presenting:

  • A clear research direction
  • Relevant academic qualifications
  • Evidence of research experience
  • Publications where applicable
  • A strong statement of purpose
  • Appropriate institutional support
  • Suitable academic references
  • A host institution that aligns with their research interests

Application Process

Applications are submitted directly to COMSTECH Headquarters in Islamabad, Pakistan.

Unlike application systems that require candidates to complete an online portal from beginning to end, this fellowship requires applicants to send their application and supporting documents by email.

Applications can be submitted to:

khazima@comstech.org

or

comstech@comstech.org

Applicants should make sure that their documents are complete before sending the application.

Documents Required

Applicants are expected to provide several supporting documents.

1. Completed application form

Applicants must complete the official COMSTECH fellowship application form.

2. Valid passport

A scanned copy of a valid passport must be included.

Applicants should ensure that the passport copy is clear and readable.

3. Curriculum vitae

Applicants must provide a CV of no more than five pages.

The CV should include relevant research experience and publications.

Applicants should focus on information that demonstrates their academic background, scientific expertise, research experience, publications, and professional achievements.

4. Supporting statement from the home institution

Applicants must provide a supporting statement from the Head of their Home Institution.

This demonstrates institutional support for the applicant’s participation in the fellowship.

5. Two reference letters

Applicants must submit two reference letters from senior scientists familiar with their work.

An important requirement is that the Head of the applicant’s Home Institution cannot serve as one of the referees.

Applicants should therefore select referees who can provide meaningful assessments of their research capabilities, scientific experience, academic potential, and professional development.

6. Academic degrees and transcripts

Applicants must provide copies of their:

  • M.S. or equivalent degree
  • Ph.D., where applicable
  • Relevant university transcripts

These documents are used to verify the applicant’s academic qualifications.

Application Deadline

There is no single fixed annual deadline stated for this fellowship.

According to the published COMSTECH information:

Applications and nominations are open all year round.

This means eligible researchers can submit applications throughout the year rather than waiting for a specific annual closing date.

However, applicants should still begin the process early because they may need to identify a suitable host institution, prepare a research proposal, obtain institutional approval, request reference letters, and gather academic and identity documents.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although the fellowship accepts applications throughout the year, applicants should not treat the open-ended application period as a reason to submit an incomplete application.

A strong application should demonstrate a clear connection between the applicant’s background, proposed research, and the expertise available at the host institution.

1. Identify the right host institution

One of the most important steps is finding a suitable CCoE member institution.

Applicants should consider:

  • The institution’s research expertise
  • Available laboratories and facilities
  • Researchers working in the applicant’s field
  • Compatibility with the proposed research
  • Availability of appropriate supervision
  • Potential for long-term collaboration

2. Develop a clear research plan

Applicants should have a well-defined research direction.

The proposed work should be realistic within the six-to-twelve-month fellowship period and should make good use of the host institution’s expertise and facilities.

3. Highlight your research experience

The CV and supporting documents should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s scientific background.

Relevant information can include:

  • Previous research projects
  • Publications
  • Academic achievements
  • Laboratory experience
  • Technical skills
  • Conferences and scientific presentations
  • Research collaborations
  • Current research activities

4. Secure strong references

Applicants should select senior scientists who know their work well and can provide detailed recommendations.

A generic reference letter may not demonstrate the applicant’s scientific potential as effectively as a specific assessment of their research abilities.

5. Obtain institutional support early

Because the Head of the Home Institution must provide a supporting statement, applicants should begin this process well before submission.

This can also help avoid delays later in the application process.

Why the Fellowship Can Be Valuable for Researchers

The COMSTECH fellowship provides researchers with the opportunity to gain experience in a different research environment while remaining connected to the broader OIC scientific community.

The six-to-twelve-month duration can allow fellows to develop substantial research experience rather than simply attending a short course or workshop.

The program can also help researchers establish relationships with scientists and institutions that may continue beyond the fellowship period.

For early-career scientists, these professional connections can be particularly important for future research collaboration, joint publications, training opportunities, and scientific networking.

Opportunities for Women Scientists

The fellowship specifically indicates that preference is given to young scientists, particularly women scientists, who are at the beginning of their research careers.

Women researchers who meet the academic, nationality, research, and age requirements should therefore consider the program when looking for opportunities to expand their international research experience.

Applicants should nevertheless understand that preference does not necessarily mean automatic selection. Fellowship awards are made based on scientific merit and the assessment of the application by COMSTECH and the relevant host institution.

Potential for Long-Term Collaboration

The fellowship is not only intended to provide temporary research training.

One of its broader objectives is to foster research linkages for further collaboration.

A successful fellowship can therefore serve as an entry point for longer-term relationships between:

  • Researchers
  • Universities
  • Research institutions
  • Laboratories
  • Centers of excellence
  • Scientific networks across OIC member states

This can be particularly useful for researchers who want to develop international research partnerships or establish connections with institutions that have specialized expertise and facilities.

Application Email Addresses

Applicants should send their completed applications and supporting documentation to one of the designated COMSTECH email addresses:

khazima@comstech.org

comstech@comstech.org

Applicants should carefully check that all required documents are attached before submitting their application.

COMSTECH Contact Information

Applicants who require clarification can contact the COMSTECH Secretariat.

COMSTECH Secretariat
33-Constitution Avenue
G-5/2
Islamabad, Pakistan

Telephone: +92 51 9220681-3

Fax: +92 51 9211115, 9220265, 9205264

Email: khazima@comstech.org / comstech@comstech.org

Application Form

The application form is available through the COMSTECH application platform referenced in the fellowship announcement.

Applicants should complete the form and submit it together with the required supporting documentation.

Apply HERE today!

Important Points to Remember

Before applying, prospective candidates should review the following requirements carefully:

  1. The fellowship is for eligible researchers connected to least developed OIC countries.
  2. The minimum qualification is M.S./Ph.D. or equivalent, depending on the level of research.
  3. The maximum age is 35 for graduate studies and 45 for post-graduate studies.
  4. The fellowship lasts 6–12 months.
  5. The research must fall within natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering, or technology.
  6. Host institutions are participating research and higher-education institutions within OIC member states.
  7. COMSTECH covers international low-cost airfare.
  8. Host institutions are expected to provide accommodation, subsistence, supervision, and local training.
  9. Applications are submitted by email to COMSTECH Headquarters.
  10. Applicants must provide a passport copy, CV, institutional support statement, two reference letters, degrees, and transcripts.
  11. The Head of the Home Institution cannot be one of the two referees.
  12. Applications and nominations are open throughout the year.
  13. Selection is based on scientific merit.
  14. Preference is given to young researchers, particularly women scientists and researchers working in least developed OIC countries.

To learn more about the COMSTECH Research Fellowship 2026, click HERE.

Conclusion

The COMSTECH Research Fellowships for Least Developed Countries in OIC offer an important pathway for eligible young scientists, engineers, and researchers to gain advanced research and training experience at centers of excellence within OIC member states.

With a fellowship duration of six to twelve months, support for international low-cost airfare, and host-institution assistance covering accommodation, subsistence, supervision, and local training, the program is designed to help researchers strengthen their scientific capabilities while building international research connections.

The fellowship is particularly relevant to early-career researchers from eligible least developed OIC countries who hold the required academic qualifications and are working in natural sciences, applied sciences, engineering, or technology.

Since applications and nominations are open throughout the year, eligible researchers do not need to wait for a conventional annual deadline. However, prospective applicants should begin preparing well in advance to identify a suitable host institution, develop a strong research plan, secure institutional support and references, and assemble all required documents.

For researchers seeking advanced scientific training, international exposure, and opportunities to establish long-term research collaborations within the OIC scientific community, this COMSTECH fellowship can provide a valuable platform for professional and academic development.

To explore and learn more about other fellowship opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the C3 EmpowerHer Program 2026, a six-month climate resilience accelerator designed to support early-stage ventures that are led by women or primarily benefit women across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).

The program is delivered by C3 – Companies Creating Change and funded by the Resilient Futures Fund (RFF). It is designed to help promising climate resilience enterprises strengthen their business models, improve their solutions, access expert guidance, develop pilots, connect with investors and ecosystem partners, and become more investment-ready.

A total of 30 startups will be selected for the program, while the top 10 startups will share USD 150,000 in catalytic grant funding, with each of the top 10 potentially receiving up to USD 20,000 for pilots and impact activities.

The six-month program is scheduled to run from October 2026 through Demo Day in the second quarter of 2027, giving participating founders an opportunity to work intensively with climate, sector, investment, and ecosystem experts.

Applications close on August 31, 2026.

C3 EmpowerHer Program 2026 at a Glance

  • Program: C3 EmpowerHer
  • Host: C3 – Companies Creating Change
  • Funding partner: Resilient Futures Fund (RFF)
  • Target region: Middle East and North Africa (MENA)
  • Target ventures: Early-stage women-led or women-benefitting climate resilience startups
  • Number of startups selected: 30
  • Catalytic grant funding: USD 150,000 distributed across the top 10 startups
  • Potential funding per top-10 startup: Up to USD 20,000
  • Program duration: Six months
  • Program period: October 2026 to Demo Day in Q2 2027
  • Application deadline: August 31, 2026
  • Core support: Workshops, mentorship, diagnostics, strategic advisory, pilot support, investor and ecosystem access
  • Demo Day: In-person showcase in Egypt in Q2 2027

What Is the C3 EmpowerHer Program?

The C3 EmpowerHer Program is a dedicated support initiative for early-stage climate resilience ventures operating across MENA.

The program focuses on enterprises developing solutions that help communities, economies, and ecosystems withstand, recover from, and thrive despite the effects of climate change.

Rather than focusing exclusively on climate mitigation, the program places particular emphasis on climate resilience. This means supporting businesses that address the practical challenges created or intensified by climate change, including water insecurity, food and agricultural challenges, extreme heat, flooding, coastal risks, infrastructure vulnerability, sustainable livelihoods, and access to climate finance.

The program also has a strong gender dimension. Eligible ventures must either be led by women or provide solutions that primarily benefit women, with gender impact intentionally incorporated into the venture’s approach.

Through six months of structured support, C3 EmpowerHer aims to help participating startups strengthen their solutions, develop market opportunities, execute pilots, and prepare for investment.

USD 150,000 in Catalytic Grant Funding

One of the most significant features of C3 EmpowerHer is its catalytic grant component.

The program will select 30 startups, with the top 10 startups receiving additional support and access to a total of USD 150,000 in catalytic grant funding.

The program states that the top 10 startups can receive up to USD 20,000 per startup to support pilots and impact.

This funding is intended to help promising ventures move beyond ideas and early validation toward practical implementation, testing, market engagement, and measurable climate and gender impact.

The catalytic nature of the funding can be particularly valuable for early-stage startups that may need additional capital to demonstrate their solutions to customers, partners, investors, and other ecosystem stakeholders.

What Does the Six-Month Program Offer?

C3 EmpowerHer is structured as a six-month hands-on support program rather than simply a grant competition.

Participating ventures can receive a combination of training, expert guidance, mentorship, strategic support, ecosystem access, and pilot development assistance.

The program runs from October 2026 through Demo Day in Q2 2027.

1. Expert-Led Training

Every startup selected for the cohort will have access to expert-led training through approximately 8 to 12 virtual workshops.

These workshops are organized across five core modules and are intended to strengthen the capabilities of participating founders and teams.

The training component can help entrepreneurs build the knowledge and practical skills required to strengthen their ventures and navigate the climate innovation ecosystem.

2. Tailored Expert Support

Startups will receive tailored guidance from experts working across:

  • Climate;
  • Relevant industry sectors;
  • Investment;
  • Business development; and
  • Related areas of venture growth.

Rather than providing identical support to every startup, the program is designed to offer guidance that responds to the specific needs and circumstances of participating ventures.

3. Mentorship and Strategic Guidance

The program includes mentorship and advisory support to help founders address challenges affecting their ventures.

This can be particularly important for early-stage businesses that have developed an MVP and achieved initial traction but require additional strategic support to move toward the next stage of growth.

4. Investor and Ecosystem Access

Participating startups will gain access to C3’s network of:

  • Venture capital firms;
  • Development finance institutions;
  • Corporates;
  • Impact funds; and
  • Other ecosystem stakeholders.

This network can potentially help participating founders build relationships with organizations that can contribute to business growth, investment, partnerships, market access, and future opportunities.

Additional Benefits for the Top 10 Startups

While all 30 selected startups will receive core program support, the top 10 startups will receive additional benefits.

These include strategic advisory sessions, catalytic pilot funding, pilot design support, and participation in an in-person Demo Day in Egypt.

Strategic Advisory Sessions

The top 10 startups will receive access to 10 expert advisory boards, alongside development of a strategic roadmap.

This additional layer of support is designed to provide more targeted guidance as the selected ventures work toward strengthening their businesses and scaling their impact.

Catalytic Pilot Funding

The top 10 startups can receive up to USD 20,000 each to support pilot projects and impact activities.

Pilot funding can be especially valuable for early-stage climate ventures because it can help bridge the gap between an early solution and broader market adoption.

Pilot Design Support

Top-performing ventures will also receive support in designing pilots.

The program indicates that these pilots will be developed with market enablers, potentially helping startups test their solutions in environments where they can demonstrate commercial and impact potential.

Demo Day in Egypt

The program will culminate in an in-person Demo Day in Egypt during Q2 2027.

This provides selected startups with an opportunity to showcase their ventures to investors and other relevant stakeholders.

For early-stage founders, such a platform can be an important opportunity to communicate their business models, demonstrate their solutions, highlight their impact, and develop relationships with potential investors and partners.

Who Should Apply?

C3 EmpowerHer is specifically designed for early-stage climate resilience ventures operating in MENA.

The program is not intended for every type of startup. Ventures should demonstrate a clear connection to both climate resilience and gender impact.

According to the program criteria, a venture should meet the following characteristics.

1. Women-Centered and Climate-Focused

The venture must either:

  • Be women-led; or
  • Provide a solution that benefits women as primary beneficiaries.

The business must also have climate resilience at the core of its mission.

The program therefore distinguishes climate resilience from businesses that focus solely on general sustainability or pure climate mitigation.

Applicants should be able to clearly demonstrate how their solution helps people, communities, businesses, or ecosystems adapt to climate-related challenges.

2. Early-Stage With Traction

The program is intended for ventures at the:

  • Pre-seed stage;
  • Seed/early-stage development; through
  • Pre-Series A stage.

Applicants should have an MVP, or minimum viable product, and early evidence of traction.

This means the program is designed for ventures that have moved beyond the purely conceptual stage.

Founders should be able to demonstrate that they have developed an initial version of their solution and have some evidence that the market, customers, beneficiaries, partners, or other stakeholders are responding to it.

3. MENA-Based or MENA-Operating

The venture must be:

  • Headquartered in MENA; or
  • Primarily operating within MENA.

This requirement makes the program specifically relevant to entrepreneurs addressing climate resilience challenges within the region.

Importantly, the source material identifies the region as MENA but does not provide a specific list of individual countries. Prospective applicants should therefore verify their country’s eligibility through the official application information before applying.

4. Intentional Gender and Climate Impact

Impact must be intentionally incorporated into the venture’s solution.

The program is looking for businesses with clear intentionality around both:

  • Gender outcomes; and
  • Climate outcomes.

Applicants should therefore be able to explain not only what their business does commercially, but also how it contributes to improving resilience and addressing challenges affecting women.

5. Commitment to the Full Program

The founding team must be prepared to commit time to the six-month program.

This includes participation in activities such as:

  • Workshops;
  • Mentorship;
  • Diagnostics;
  • Strategic support;
  • Pilot execution; and
  • Other program activities.

Founders should therefore ensure that their teams have sufficient availability to participate meaningfully throughout the program.

C3 EmpowerHer Focus Areas

The program identifies several key climate resilience areas where it is seeking solutions.

These focus areas include:

Water and Sanitation

Solutions addressing water availability, water security, sanitation challenges, and climate-related pressures on water systems.

Food and Agri-Climate

Innovations addressing food security and the effects of climate change on agriculture and food systems.

This may include solutions designed to help agricultural communities adapt to changing climate conditions and strengthen food-system resilience.

Heat Resilience

Solutions helping people, communities, businesses, and infrastructure respond to increasing heat and extreme temperature conditions.

Coastal and Flood Adaptation

Businesses developing solutions for communities and ecosystems exposed to flooding, coastal risks, and other climate-related hazards.

Nature-Based Solutions

Innovations that use or work with natural systems to address climate resilience challenges.

Climate-Resilient Infrastructure

Solutions aimed at making infrastructure more capable of withstanding climate-related risks and disruptions.

Sustainable Livelihoods

Enterprises helping communities develop livelihoods that are more resilient and sustainable in the face of climate change.

Climate Finance Access

Solutions designed to improve access to financing for climate resilience activities, particularly where financial barriers prevent communities or businesses from adopting climate solutions.

Why Climate Resilience Matters for MENA

The C3 EmpowerHer Program is focused on a region where climate resilience is increasingly important to communities, businesses, infrastructure, food systems, and natural ecosystems.

The program’s focus on areas such as water and sanitation, agriculture, heat resilience, coastal adaptation, infrastructure, livelihoods, and climate finance reflects the broad range of challenges that climate change can create for societies and economies.

By supporting early-stage ventures, the program seeks to strengthen businesses that are developing practical solutions to these challenges.

The gender focus is equally significant because the program specifically seeks ventures that place women at the center of climate resilience solutions, either through women-led entrepreneurship or solutions designed primarily to benefit women.

Why Startups Should Consider Applying

There are several reasons why an eligible climate resilience startup may find C3 EmpowerHer valuable.

Access to Specialized Expertise

Climate startups often need advice that goes beyond traditional business development.

The program connects participants with experts in climate, relevant sectors, and investment, giving founders an opportunity to receive guidance tailored to their challenges.

Strengthening Business Readiness

Early-stage ventures may have promising technologies or solutions but still need to strengthen their business models, market strategies, operations, and investment readiness.

The program is designed to help founders address these areas through structured support.

Opportunity to Develop Pilots

For the top 10 startups, access to pilot funding and pilot design support can help transform an early-stage solution into a real-world demonstration.

A successful pilot can potentially provide evidence that can later be used when engaging customers, partners, investors, and other stakeholders.

Investor and Ecosystem Connections

Access to investors and ecosystem partners can be particularly important for startups seeking to move from early traction toward additional capital and market opportunities.

Through C3’s network, participants can potentially connect with venture capital firms, development finance institutions, corporations, and impact funds.

International Visibility

The Demo Day in Egypt provides the top 10 startups with a platform to showcase their ventures to investors.

For founders seeking investment or strategic partnerships, the opportunity to present their solutions to relevant stakeholders can be an important component of their growth journey.

Program Timeline

The C3 EmpowerHer Program is expected to operate over approximately six months.

The program begins in October 2026 and continues through Demo Day in Q2 2027.

The general progression includes:

  1. Selection of the 30 participating startups.
  2. Program commencement in October 2026.
  3. Expert-led virtual workshops.
  4. Tailored mentorship and advisory support.
  5. Diagnostics and strategic development.
  6. Pilot design and implementation support for the top 10 startups.
  7. Catalytic funding for qualifying top-10 ventures.
  8. Investor and ecosystem engagement.
  9. Demo Day in Egypt in Q2 2027.

Applicants should be prepared to remain actively engaged throughout the six-month period.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the C3 EmpowerHer Program is:

August 31, 2026

Entrepreneurs should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Early preparation gives founders enough time to review their eligibility, prepare information about their startup, articulate their climate and gender impact, and ensure that the application accurately reflects their venture.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Eligible founders should consider several important elements when preparing their application.

Clearly Explain the Climate Problem

Your application should make it easy to understand the climate challenge your venture is addressing.

Explain:

  • What problem exists?
  • Who experiences the problem?
  • How is climate change contributing to or worsening it?
  • Why is the problem important?
  • Why does your solution matter?

Demonstrate Your MVP and Traction

Because C3 EmpowerHer targets early-stage ventures with an MVP and evidence of traction, applicants should clearly communicate where their startup currently stands.

Where applicable, founders should be prepared to demonstrate:

  • Development of their MVP;
  • Customer engagement;
  • User adoption;
  • Revenue or commercial activity;
  • Partnerships;
  • Pilot activity;
  • Market interest; or
  • Other evidence of traction.

Explain the Gender Impact

The gender component should be clearly articulated.

If the startup is women-led, applicants should clearly demonstrate this.

If the startup is women-benefitting, founders should explain how women are the primary beneficiaries and what measurable or intended outcomes the solution creates for them.

Demonstrate Climate Resilience

Applicants should make the connection between their product or service and climate resilience explicit.

Do not assume that reviewers will automatically understand the climate relevance of the business.

Explain how the venture helps communities, economies, or ecosystems prepare for, withstand, recover from, or adapt to climate-related challenges.

Explain Why You Need the Program

Strong applicants should be able to identify the specific challenges for which C3 EmpowerHer support would be valuable.

These could include:

  • Investment readiness;
  • Pilot development;
  • Market access;
  • Strategic planning;
  • Technical expertise;
  • Climate-sector expertise;
  • Investor connections;
  • Business model development; or
  • Scaling challenges.

Demonstrate Commitment

Since the program requires a significant time commitment over six months, founders should demonstrate that their core team is ready to participate fully.

What the Resilient Futures Fund Does

C3 EmpowerHer is funded by the Resilient Futures Fund (RFF).

According to the program information, the Resilient Futures Fund aims to strengthen resilience and increase opportunities for climate solutions that are led by, involve, or benefit women and girls.

The fund provides catalytic capital and support to climate solutions aligned with these objectives.

The fund is managed by 2X Global and supported by Amazon, Reckitt, the Skoll Foundation, the UPS Foundation, and the Visa Foundation.

The program information directs interested readers to the Resilient Futures Fund’s official information for further details.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is C3 EmpowerHer?

C3 EmpowerHer is a six-month program supporting early-stage women-led or women-benefitting climate resilience ventures across MENA.

How many startups will be selected?

The program will select 30 startups.

How much grant funding is available?

A total of USD 150,000 in catalytic grant funding will be distributed across the top 10 startups.

How much can one startup receive?

Each of the top 10 startups can receive up to USD 20,000 for pilots and impact activities.

What stage should the startup be at?

The program is designed for early-stage ventures from pre-seed to pre-Series A, with an MVP and early evidence of traction.

Does the startup need to be focused on climate resilience?

Yes. Climate resilience should be central to the venture’s mission. The program specifically distinguishes its focus from solutions focused purely on mitigation.

Does the venture need to have a gender component?

Yes. The venture must either be women-led or provide a solution that benefits women as primary beneficiaries, with intentional gender impact incorporated into the solution.

Where should the startup operate?

The venture must be headquartered in or primarily operating within MENA.

How long is the program?

The program lasts six months, beginning in October 2026 and continuing through Demo Day in Q2 2027.

APPLY HERE

Is the program entirely in person?

The source states that the program includes 8–12 virtual workshops, while the Demo Day in Egypt is an in-person showcase. The supplied information does not provide enough detail to state that every component is entirely virtual or entirely in person.

When is the application deadline?

Applications close on August 31, 2026.

Visit HERE for more information about the C3 EmpowerHer Program 2026.

Final Conclusion

The C3 EmpowerHer Program 2026 presents a substantial opportunity for early-stage climate resilience entrepreneurs working across the Middle East and North Africa.

With 30 startups set to participate, the program combines expert-led training, tailored mentorship, strategic advisory support, investor and ecosystem access, pilot development, and opportunities to connect with major climate and investment stakeholders.

The opportunity becomes particularly significant for the top 10 startups, which can benefit from additional strategic advisory support, pilot design assistance, an opportunity to participate in market-enabling pilots, and access to USD 150,000 in catalytic grant funding, with individual grants of up to USD 20,000.

For entrepreneurs working on water and sanitation, food and agricultural resilience, extreme heat, coastal and flood adaptation, nature-based solutions, resilient infrastructure, sustainable livelihoods, or climate finance access, C3 EmpowerHer offers a structured pathway to strengthen both their ventures and their climate impact.

The program’s deliberate emphasis on women-led and women-benefitting solutions also makes it particularly relevant to founders developing climate resilience innovations with strong gender outcomes.

Eligible founders should begin preparing their applications early and ensure they can clearly demonstrate their startup’s MVP, early traction, MENA connection, climate resilience focus, gender impact, and commitment to the six-month program.

Application deadline: August 31, 2026.

For more global Grant opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Audible has launched an open call for nonprofit organizations across the United States that are working directly with young people and are interested in using the power of audio storytelling to strengthen youth development, literacy, discovery, and engagement.

Through this initiative, Audible is seeking small to mid-sized nonprofit organizations that already provide structured programming for underrepresented young people between the ages of 12 and 18. Selected organizations will receive grant funding of $20,000 to $40,000, complimentary Audible memberships for participating youth, implementation support, and other resources to help integrate audio experiences into existing youth programs.

The initiative is designed around the idea that audio stories can help young people discover new perspectives, imagine different possibilities, develop a stronger love of listening, and see themselves and the wider world in new ways.

About the Audible Open Call

Audible is inviting eligible nonprofit and nongovernmental organizations in the United States to collaborate on youth development programming that incorporates intentional listening experiences.

The initiative is not simply a funding opportunity. Audible intends to work directly with selected organizations to help them incorporate audio content into their existing programs and create meaningful, recurring opportunities for young people to listen, explore, discuss, and discover.

Participating organizations will be expected to integrate Audible into their existing programming rather than create an entirely separate initiative. The proposed programming should include intentional activities such as workshops, listening sessions, and guided exploration of audio content.

Organizations should also be prepared to maintain regular engagement with participating youth, with a minimum of biweekly touchpoints throughout the program.

What Audible Is Looking For

The open call is specifically aimed at organizations with established youth-development or literacy programming.

Eligible organizations should generally:

  • Be small to mid-sized nonprofit or nongovernmental organizations operating in the United States.
  • Directly serve between 150 and 300 underrepresented young people.
  • Serve young people between 12 and 18 years old through the proposed program.
  • Provide programming outside formal school settings.
  • Operate structured and recurring programs such as after-school initiatives, community centers, youth-development programs, or literacy-focused programs.
  • Have established relationships with the young people they currently serve.
  • Be able to integrate Audible into existing programming.
  • Have the capacity to support youth in accessing and using Audible.
  • Be willing to collect meaningful information about participation, engagement, and outcomes.
  • Share relevant findings and lessons learned with Audible.
  • Have appropriate youth-data protection and privacy procedures.

Importantly, organizations do not need to have previously used audio content in their programs. Audible states that experience with audio is not a prerequisite because selected organizations will receive onboarding support and implementation resources.

Grant Funding of $20,000 to $40,000

One of the major components of this opportunity is direct grant funding.

Selected organizations can receive between $20,000 and $40,000, with the specific amount determined according to the scope of the proposed program and the number of young people reached.

The funding is intended to support program design and delivery, allowing participating organizations to incorporate audio-based experiences into their existing youth-development activities.

Applicants may also include overhead costs in their proposed budgets, with overhead permitted at approximately 10% of the total grant request.

What Selected Organizations Will Receive

Organizations selected for the collaboration will receive several forms of support beyond the grant itself.

1. Grant funding

Selected organizations will receive financial support ranging from $20,000 to $40,000.

The final grant amount will depend on the proposed program’s scope and youth reach.

2. Complimentary Audible memberships

Participating young people will receive access to complimentary Audible memberships.

This gives organizations an opportunity to introduce youth to a broad range of audio content and incorporate listening into their existing activities.

3. Onboarding and implementation support

Audible will provide resources and onboarding assistance to help selected organizations introduce the platform effectively.

This is particularly relevant for organizations that have not previously incorporated audio content into their programming.

4. Shared metrics framework

Measuring impact is an important part of the collaboration.

Selected organizations will work with Audible around a shared framework for tracking engagement and outcomes. This means organizations should be prepared to collect relevant program data and contribute insights about how young people interact with audio content.

5. Public recognition

Selected organizations will receive public recognition as part of Audible’s official program launch.

This may provide participating organizations with additional visibility around their youth-development work and their collaboration with Audible.

6. Potential multi-year collaboration

Audible intends to explore the possibility of developing successful collaborations into multi-year partnerships.

Organizations demonstrating strong youth engagement and measurable impact may therefore have the potential to continue working with Audible beyond the initial six-month program period.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for nonprofit and nongovernmental organizations operating in the United States.

Organizations may include entities such as qualifying 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(4) organizations.

Applicants should already have an established youth program and existing relationships with the young people they serve. This is important because Audible is not primarily looking for organizations that intend to recruit an entirely new group of participants for the initiative.

Instead, the organization should already have a functioning program and be able to incorporate Audible into that existing structure.

Youth Served Through the Program

The proposed program must specifically serve young people between the ages of 12 and 18.

Organizations that serve people outside this age range can still apply, provided that the particular programming proposed for the Audible collaboration focuses on youth aged 12 to 18.

The broader organization therefore does not necessarily have to serve only teenagers. The important requirement is that the youth participating in the proposed collaboration fall within the required age range.

Focus on Underrepresented Youth

Audible defines underrepresented youth broadly and recognizes that the nature of underrepresentation can differ between communities.

According to the opportunity information, this can include young people who identify as part of communities such as:

  • Black, Indigenous, and other people of color
  • Asian or Asian American communities
  • Latinx or Hispanic communities
  • LGBTQIA+ communities
  • Women and girls
  • Young people with disabilities
  • Neurodivergent young people
  • Young people who do not identify as part of the majority community in their place of residence

Applicants are encouraged to explain the particular barriers, inequalities, or challenges experienced by the young people they serve rather than relying solely on a broad label.

Existing Relationships With Young People Are Important

One of the eligibility requirements is that an organization must already have established relationships with the young people it serves.

This means applicants should demonstrate that they already operate meaningful programs for their target population.

The opportunity is therefore particularly relevant to established youth-development organizations, community organizations, literacy organizations, and similar nonprofits with ongoing programming.

Organizations whose only plan is to recruit an entirely new population specifically for this initiative may not meet the intended eligibility requirements.

Programs Should Take Place Outside Formal School Settings

The initiative is focused on youth programming outside traditional formal school environments.

Examples can include:

  • After-school programs
  • Community centers
  • Youth-development organizations
  • Literacy programs
  • Structured community-based youth initiatives
  • Other recurring youth programs outside formal school settings

K-12 institutions are not generally eligible to apply as schools. However, the opportunity information states that a K-12 institution with 501(c)(3) status and the ability to accept private funds may apply.

Six-Month Program Capacity

Organizations must have the capacity to onboard participating youth onto Audible, provide technical support, and maintain engagement throughout a six-month term.

Applicants should therefore consider whether their existing staffing, infrastructure, technology, and youth-support systems are sufficient to manage the collaboration.

The organization should also be prepared to maintain recurring engagement, including a minimum of biweekly touchpoints.

Measuring Impact and Collecting Data

Impact measurement is a central component of the initiative.

Audible is looking for organizations that are willing to collect meaningful information about youth engagement and outcomes and share those insights as part of the collaboration.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to think beyond simply providing young people with access to audio content.

A strong proposal should explain how listening experiences will be incorporated into programming and how the organization will determine whether the initiative is producing meaningful engagement or outcomes.

Organizations must also have data-protection and privacy procedures in place, or the capacity to develop them, to support compliance with COPPA and the secure handling of youth information.

Can Organizations That Have Never Used Audio Apply?

Yes.

Previous experience using audio content is not required.

Audible specifically indicates that organizations with strong youth programming foundations and established relationships with young people can apply even if they do not currently use audio content.

Selected organizations will receive onboarding support and resources to help them incorporate Audible into their existing programs.

This makes the opportunity potentially relevant to organizations that have strong youth-development infrastructure but are looking to introduce a new method of engagement through storytelling and listening.

Can Multiple Organizations From the Same Area Apply?

Yes.

Multiple organizations operating within the same geographic region can submit applications.

Each organization will be evaluated independently, meaning organizations should focus on presenting the strengths, needs, programming model, youth population, and expected impact of their own proposed collaboration.

Geographic Eligibility

This opportunity is not open worldwide.

The application round is specifically open to qualifying nonprofit and nongovernmental organizations operating in the United States.

Therefore, organizations based exclusively outside the United States are not eligible for this particular opportunity based on the published criteria.

There is no requirement in the information provided for applicants to come from a particular U.S. state or region. Eligible organizations can apply regardless of their geographic location within the United States.

Important Restrictions

Applicants should carefully review the terms and eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

Organizations must have appropriate data-protection and privacy procedures, or the ability to develop them, particularly because the program involves young people and youth data.

In addition, organizations must not have a primary political or religious affiliation that would direct the use of grant funds.

All grants remain subject to Audible’s discretion, and applicants are required to review and accept the applicable terms and conditions as part of the application process.

Application Process

The application process consists of two stages.

Stage 1: Full proposal

Eligible organizations first submit a full proposal through the application platform.

The proposal should demonstrate that the organization meets the eligibility criteria and explain how Audible will be incorporated into the organization’s existing youth programming.

Stage 2: Finalist conversation

Organizations that progress in the selection process will participate in a 60-minute conversation with the Audible team.

This provides finalists with an opportunity to discuss their proposed program and potentially provide additional information about their organization, youth population, implementation approach, and expected impact.

Application Deadline

Applications opened on June 12, 2026 and closed on July 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

Selected organizations were expected to be notified by late August 2026, with programming scheduled to begin in October 2026.

Important: Because the stated deadline was July 31, 2026, this application round is now closed as of August 11, 2026.

Application Link

The original application was available through Audible’s application platform:

Audible Open Call Application

Organizations interested in future rounds or similar Audible initiatives should monitor Audible’s official communications for new application opportunities.

Apply HERE today!

Why This Opportunity Matters

The Audible open call represents an approach to youth development that combines funding, technology, storytelling, and structured engagement.

For eligible organizations, the opportunity goes beyond receiving a grant. Selected nonprofits can gain access to audio content, implementation resources, a shared impact-measurement framework, and the possibility of developing a longer-term collaboration.

The initiative also recognizes that young people engage with stories in different ways. Audio can provide an accessible format through which young people encounter new ideas, perspectives, experiences, and voices.

For organizations already working with underrepresented youth, incorporating structured listening experiences into existing programming could provide another tool for encouraging discovery and engagement.

How Organizations Can Prepare for Similar Opportunities

Although this particular application round has closed, organizations interested in future opportunities of this type can use the published requirements as a preparation checklist.

1. Maintain strong youth-program records

Organizations should maintain clear records showing the number of young people served, their age ranges, program participation, and engagement.

2. Build established community relationships

Strong relationships with the young people and communities an organization serves can be important when applying for collaborative funding opportunities.

3. Develop measurable outcomes

Organizations should be able to explain what they are trying to achieve and how they will measure progress.

4. Strengthen data-protection practices

Programs involving minors should have appropriate privacy and data-protection procedures.

5. Consider how new technology can complement existing programs

Organizations do not necessarily need to build entirely new programs whenever a new funding opportunity becomes available. Opportunities such as this one can favor organizations that can thoughtfully integrate new tools into established programming.

6. Prepare a clear implementation strategy

A strong proposal should demonstrate how funding and resources will translate into meaningful activities for participants.

To lean more about the Audible Grant 2026, click HERE.

Conclusion

The Audible Open Call was designed to support U.S.-based nonprofits that are already working directly with underrepresented young people and want to incorporate audio storytelling into their youth-development or literacy programming.

Selected organizations were eligible for $20,000 to $40,000 in grant funding, complimentary Audible memberships for participating youth, onboarding and implementation support, a shared metrics framework, public recognition, and the potential for longer-term collaboration.

The program focused on organizations serving 150 to 300 young people ages 12 to 18 through structured programming outside formal school settings. Applicants also needed established relationships with the youth they serve, the capacity to sustain a six-month program, and a commitment to measuring and sharing impact.

The application deadline was July 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET, meaning this particular round has now closed. Organizations that meet the criteria should nevertheless watch for future Audible initiatives and prepare their programs, impact data, youth-engagement strategies, and organizational documentation ahead of future funding rounds.

To explore and learn more about other grant opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.
