item.content:encoded:
The University of British Columbia is offering its prestigious Four Year Doctoral Fellowship to outstanding domestic and international doctoral students. Commonly known as the UBC 4YF, the fellowship provides stable financial support so that recipients can concentrate on advanced research and successfully complete their doctoral studies at UBC’s Vancouver campus.

Effective September 2026, recipients without external scholarship funding can receive an annual stipend of up to CAD 24,000, together with tuition support, for up to four years. This represents potential stipend funding of CAD 96,000 over four years, in addition to applicable tuition coverage.

There is no separate application for the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship. Candidates seeking admission to an eligible PhD, Doctor of Musical Arts or combined MD/PhD program are automatically considered after submitting their graduate admission application.

The application deadline is determined separately by each UBC graduate program. Prospective students must therefore check the deadline for their chosen doctoral program rather than rely on a single university-wide date.

UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship: Key Information

Item Details
Host institution University of British Columbia
Campus Vancouver Campus, Canada
Fellowship name Four Year Doctoral Fellowship
Abbreviation 4YF
Degree levels PhD, DMA and the PhD portion of MD/PhD programs
Annual stipend Up to CAD 24,000 from September 2026
Tuition support Tuition award applied against applicable tuition charges
Maximum duration Up to four years, subject to applicable limits
Eligible nationalities Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students
Study status Full-time
Selection basis Academic excellence and graduate-program recommendation
Separate fellowship application Not normally required
Deadline Determined by each UBC graduate program

What Is the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship?

The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is a major institutional funding programme administered by the University of British Columbia’s Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies.

The programme is designed to help UBC attract and retain exceptionally strong doctoral candidates from Canada and other countries. It gives recipients a stable base level of financial support during their doctoral studies and research.

The fellowship is principally intended for students beginning the first year of an eligible full-time doctoral program. However, UBC graduate programs may also select outstanding continuing doctoral students.

Each graduate program receives a limited allocation of Four Year Fellowships. The program reviews its incoming and continuing students and recommends its strongest candidates, normally giving priority to new students.

Receiving admission to UBC does not guarantee a Four Year Doctoral Fellowship. All eligible admitted applicants are considered, but only the highest-ranked candidates selected by their respective graduate programs receive offers.

UBC 4YF Financial Benefits

Beginning September 1, 2026, a 4YF recipient who does not hold another major scholarship may receive:

  • A stipend of up to CAD 24,000 per year
  • A tuition award applied against the recipient’s tuition charges
  • Funding for up to four years, subject to eligibility and program limits
  • Stable financial support for full-time doctoral research
  • Continued designation as a 4YF holder when certain external or internal awards temporarily replace the UBC stipend

A recipient funded for the complete four-year period could receive up to CAD 96,000 in stipend support, plus applicable tuition support.

The previous maximum annual stipend was CAD 18,200. UBC’s revised CAD 24,000 annual value takes effect on September 1, 2026 and applies to both new and continuing eligible 4YF recipients from that date onward.

How the Tuition Support Works

UBC describes the fellowship as providing tuition coverage, but technically, recipients do not receive a tuition waiver. Instead, a tuition award equal to the applicable tuition assessment is credited against their tuition charges.

For students enrolled in standard doctoral programs, this normally provides coverage corresponding to the assessed tuition. However, several conditions can affect the final tuition award:

  • Students in specialized doctoral programs with higher tuition assessments may receive an award capped at the tuition charged for a standard PhD program.
  • Tuition support may be reduced when combined with certain major internal or external scholarships.
  • If a recipient’s tuition is already paid by a third-party sponsor or through a staff tuition waiver, the 4YF tuition award may be reduced accordingly.
  • Indigenous students receiving eligible Band funding are treated under a stated exception and may remain eligible for tuition awards.
  • Funding rules can change depending on the value and source of another award.

Applicants should therefore understand “tuition coverage” within the conditions established in the official UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship Guidelines.

Available Funding Period

A Four Year Doctoral Fellowship may support a recipient for a maximum of four years.

However, the actual funding period may be shorter in certain circumstances. The general limit is:

  • Four years of combined 4YF, eligible external scholarship and university-wide internal scholarship status; or
  • The end of the student’s fifth year in the doctoral program;

whichever occurs first.

An incoming doctoral student who starts the 4YF at the beginning of their program may receive the complete four-year period. A continuing student who receives the award later may have a shorter funding period because funding normally cannot extend beyond the applicable fifth-year limit.

For students who transfer directly from a master’s program into a PhD without completing the master’s degree, the 4YF eligibility period is counted from the date of transfer into the doctoral program.

Eligible Degree Programs

The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship may be held by students enrolled full-time in the following degree categories:

  • Doctor of Philosophy programs
  • Doctor of Musical Arts programs
  • Combined MD/PhD programs during the PhD component

The fellowship is not generally intended for ordinary master’s programs, non-doctoral degrees or part-time study.

A student who transfers from a doctoral program into a master’s or another non-doctoral program will lose eligibility, and the award will be prorated to the effective date of the transfer.

Who Is Eligible for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship?

The fellowship is open to both domestic and international students.

Eligible applicants and students may include:

  • Canadian citizens
  • Canadian permanent residents
  • International students from any country
  • New applicants seeking admission to an eligible doctoral program
  • Continuing UBC doctoral students selected by their graduate program
  • Full-time PhD students
  • Full-time DMA students
  • Full-time MD/PhD students during the PhD portion of their studies

The award page does not establish a separate minimum GPA specifically for the 4YF. Nevertheless, selection is based on academic excellence, and competition is strong.

Applicants must also satisfy the admission requirements of their chosen doctoral program. Requirements may include:

  • Appropriate previous university qualifications
  • Strong academic transcripts
  • Evidence of research ability
  • Relevant academic or professional experience
  • A research proposal or statement of intent
  • Letters of recommendation
  • English-language proficiency
  • GRE, GMAT or other assessments where required by the selected program
  • Confirmation of a suitable research supervisor in programs where supervisor approval is necessary

Meeting the minimum admission requirements does not guarantee admission or fellowship selection.

Selection Criteria

The principal selection criterion for the UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is academic excellence.

Graduate programs may consider factors such as:

  • Academic results
  • Quality and relevance of previous qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications and conference participation
  • Academic references
  • Research potential
  • Proposed field of study
  • Alignment with faculty expertise
  • Awards and previous distinctions
  • Professional accomplishments
  • Ability to contribute to the graduate program
  • Overall strength of the admission application

UBC does not conduct one centralized competition in which every applicant is ranked together. Each eligible graduate program reviews its own students and applicants using its allocated number of fellowship places.

Is a Separate 4YF Application Required?

A separate Four Year Doctoral Fellowship application is not normally required.

To be considered, prospective students must submit an application for admission to an eligible UBC graduate program. Every PhD, DMA and MD/PhD applicant who receives an admission offer is automatically considered for 4YF funding.

The general process is:

  1. Select an eligible UBC doctoral program.
  2. Review the program’s academic and English-language requirements.
  3. Identify its application, transcript and referee deadlines.
  4. Prepare and submit the graduate admission application.
  5. Upload the required transcripts and supporting documents.
  6. Ensure referees submit their recommendations by the applicable deadline.
  7. Wait for the graduate program’s admission and funding decision.
  8. If selected, respond to the fellowship offer according to the instructions in the offer letter.
  9. Accept the formal online award offer issued through UBC Workday.

Applicants should not submit the University Award Recommendation Form themselves. That form is completed by the graduate program after it has selected a recipient.

Application Deadline

There is no single university-wide deadline for the Four Year Doctoral Fellowship.

The official deadline is:

Set by each UBC graduate program

Because fellowship consideration is connected to the doctoral admission application, candidates must submit their admission materials by the deadline for their chosen program.

UBC advises that deadlines for September admission can range from November of the preceding year to April of the intake year. Exact dates can differ for Canadian and international applicants.

Graduate programs may establish separate dates for:

  • Submission of the admission application
  • Uploading official transcript scans
  • Submission of letters of reference
  • Completion of other program-specific requirements

Candidates should consult the UBC Graduate Degree Program Listing for the exact deadline applicable to their program and nationality status.

UBC states that an application may not be considered if the application deadline is missed. Applicants should also note that changes cannot normally be made after the application has been submitted.

Nomination and Fellowship Allocation

UBC allocates a limited number of fellowship places to disciplinary faculties and graduate programs each year.

The nomination process works as follows:

  1. The Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies allocates 4YF places to disciplinary faculties.
  2. The faculties distribute their allocations among eligible graduate programs.
  3. Each graduate program reviews eligible incoming and continuing students.
  4. The program selects its strongest candidates, normally prioritizing incoming students.
  5. The selected candidate receives an initial offer from the graduate program.
  6. The program submits a University Award Recommendation Form to Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies.
  7. UBC creates a formal online award offer through Workday.
  8. The selected student accepts the award online.

Graduate programs are asked to submit their recommendations at least eight weeks before the intended start date to allow sufficient time for processing.

Possible Fellowship Start Dates

For candidates selected directly by a graduate program, the start date is determined by that program.

The available start dates are generally:

  • May 1
  • September 1
  • January 1

Recipients selected through certain university-wide or external competitions may have different start-date arrangements.

Ways a Student Can Become a 4YF Recipient

Students may receive 4YF status through several routes.

Selection by a graduate program

A UBC graduate program can select an eligible incoming or continuing student from its allocated fellowship places. This is commonly identified as a 4YF-G award.

Major internal UBC awards

Eligible recipients of certain major university-wide awards, including the Killam Doctoral Scholarship or Li Tze Fong Fellowship, may automatically become 4YF recipients.

Eligible Tri-Agency doctoral funding

Students receiving eligible doctoral-level Canadian Tri-Agency funding may automatically obtain 4YF designation. The current guidelines identify the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship–Doctoral and refer to the discontinued Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarship in connection with previous awards.

Indigenous Graduate Fellowship arrangements

Under specified circumstances, eligible students receiving an Indigenous Graduate Fellowship may receive 4YF-I status. The precise arrangement depends on whether the student already held, or had been promised, a graduate-program 4YF allocation.

These different routes can affect the source and timing of stipend payments, but recipients retain 4YF status according to the applicable rules.

Combining the 4YF With Other Scholarships

Recipients must disclose and accept eligible major internal or external scholarship funding.

The general principle is that the 4YF does not simply stack in full on top of every other major scholarship.

If another scholarship is worth more than the 4YF stipend:

  • The recipient normally receives the larger scholarship.
  • The 4YF stipend is not paid during the overlapping period.
  • The student may retain 4YF designation.
  • 4YF funding may resume after the other scholarship ends, subject to the overall duration limits.

If another scholarship is worth less than the 4YF stipend:

  • The student may receive the difference between the other scholarship and the 4YF stipend.

Recipients may generally hold the 4YF together with:

  • Graduate Support Initiative funding
  • Awards recommended directly by the graduate program
  • Graduate research assistantship stipend funding
  • Certain other forms of departmental support

Specific combinations remain subject to UBC’s award rules.

Requirement to Apply for Other Funding

4YF recipients are expected to apply for external doctoral funding when eligible.

The current guidelines state that 4YF-G and 4YF-U recipients—including Canadian, permanent-resident and international recipients—are expected to apply annually for Tri-Agency doctoral funding if they satisfy the eligibility conditions.

Failure to apply when eligible may affect continued eligibility for the 4YF or other UBC award funding.

Because Canadian Tri-Agency programmes have their own citizenship and residency rules, not every international student will necessarily be eligible to apply.

Academic Progress Requirements

Fellowship funding is conditional on satisfactory academic progress.

All 4YF recipients must submit an annual progress report, including recipients who are temporarily holding another scholarship instead of receiving the 4YF stipend.

The progress-report deadline depends on the fellowship start date:

Fellowship start date Annual progress-report deadline
May March 15
September June 1
January November 15

Failure to submit a satisfactory progress report can result in award payments being suspended.

How Fellowship Payments Are Made

UBC normally pays the stipend through Workday at the beginning of each academic term:

  • September
  • January
  • May

Payments are first applied against outstanding tuition and fees. Any remaining amount is issued to the student through electronic funds transfer, where properly configured, or by cheque.

Tuition awards are also applied through Workday at the start of each term.

Taxation of the Fellowship

UBC does not withhold income tax from the fellowship’s stipend or tuition payments.

The university issues a T4A tax form listing the stipend and tuition portions. Recipients are responsible for determining and meeting their Canadian tax-filing obligations.

International recipients should obtain appropriate tax guidance based on their individual circumstances.

Employment While Holding the Fellowship

The fellowship guidelines do not impose the previous general restriction limiting employment to an average of 12 hours per week for students holding awards of CAD 17,500 or more annually.

Nevertheless, 4YF recipients are expected to devote full-time effort to the studies or research for which they are funded. They must continue to make satisfactory academic progress.

Students should discuss substantial outside-employment commitments with their graduate program to ensure that the work does not interfere with their doctoral responsibilities.

Internships and Fellowship Interruptions

A recipient may continue to receive 4YF funding during a paid or unpaid internship or co-op placement when:

  • The student remains registered in the doctoral program; and
  • The internship or co-op is a required part of the program.

When an internship is not an academic requirement, the recipient may request an interruption of fellowship payments. If approved, the fellowship end date may be extended, normally without extending beyond the fifth year of doctoral study.

Recipients considering an internship or non-academic interruption should obtain approval before changing their study or funding arrangements.

Leave, Withdrawal and Completion

The fellowship may be affected when a recipient takes leave, withdraws or completes the degree.

Academic leave

Recipients are not normally eligible to receive 4YF payments during terms in which they are officially on leave. Payments can be suspended and the original end date extended by the approved leave period.

Program completion

Funding is prorated to the end of the month in which the student completes the doctoral program, normally when the final thesis is accepted.

Withdrawal

If a student withdraws, the award is prorated to the effective withdrawal date. Any overpayment relating to a period after completion or withdrawal must be repaid.

Transfer to another degree

A student who transfers to a master’s or another non-doctoral program loses eligibility. Transfers between closely related UBC doctoral programs may be approved without loss of funding.

Why the UBC 4YF Is a Significant Doctoral Opportunity

The Four Year Doctoral Fellowship offers several important advantages:

  • Up to four years of predictable financial support
  • An annual stipend of up to CAD 24,000 from September 2026
  • Tuition support for domestic and international recipients
  • No separate fellowship application for doctoral applicants
  • Automatic consideration after an eligible admission offer
  • Availability across a wide range of doctoral disciplines
  • Eligibility for international students
  • Possibility of combining the award with research assistantship or departmental funding
  • Recognition as a 4YF holder on the student’s UBC record
  • Greater ability to focus on doctoral research

However, applicants should not assume that admission automatically produces a fellowship. Each program has a limited allocation, and selection is reserved for its strongest candidates.

Important Application Advice

Prospective applicants should:

  1. Select a doctoral program that closely matches their academic and research background.
  2. Check the exact program deadline well in advance.
  3. Determine whether international and domestic applicants have different deadlines.
  4. Identify a suitable research supervisor when required.
  5. Prepare a focused and well-developed research proposal.
  6. Request academic references early.
  7. Demonstrate research potential through previous work, publications, dissertations or projects.
  8. Explain how the proposed research aligns with UBC expertise.
  9. Submit all documents before the relevant deadlines.
  10. Avoid treating minimum admission eligibility as evidence that fellowship selection is likely.

Because the award is based on academic excellence, the overall quality of the doctoral admission application is crucial.

Official Application and Information Links

  • UBC Four Year Doctoral Fellowship page
  • Official 4YF Guidelines
  • UBC Graduate Application and Admission Information

Conclusion

The University of British Columbia Four Year Doctoral Fellowship is a highly competitive funding opportunity for exceptional domestic and international doctoral students.

Effective September 2026, eligible recipients can receive an annual stipend of up to CAD 24,000 together with tuition support for as long as four years. Funding is available to full-time PhD and DMA students and to MD/PhD students during the doctoral component of their programs.

Prospective students do not normally submit a separate fellowship application. Instead, they apply for admission to an eligible UBC doctoral program and are automatically considered if offered admission. Graduate programs then select their strongest incoming and continuing students based primarily on academic excellence.

Because there is no universal fellowship deadline, applicants must follow the admission deadline established by their chosen graduate program. Early preparation, strong academic evidence, a compelling research plan and close alignment with the selected UBC program are essential for competitive consideration.

item.content:encoded:
The Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from accomplished professionals and emerging leaders working in the fields of peace, reconciliation, conflict transformation, and related areas. Hosted through Yale University’s International Leadership Center, the fellowship is designed to bring together an exceptional and geographically diverse group of practitioners who are contributing to peacebuilding and reconciliation in different parts of the world.

The fellowship provides participants with an opportunity to strengthen their professional leadership capacity, engage with people from different cultures and professional backgrounds, expand their international networks, and participate in an intensive program that combines virtual engagement with in-person convenings in the United States and the United Kingdom.

Admission to the Yale Peace Fellowship is highly competitive. The program seeks applicants who have already demonstrated meaningful accomplishments in the field of peace and reconciliation and who have the leadership potential, experience, and commitment necessary to contribute to an international community of peacebuilding practitioners.

For the 2027 Yale Peace Fellowship, applications are being accepted until September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications at least 24 hours before the deadline because the program does not provide extensions.

Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 at a Glance

Opportunity Yale Peace Fellowship 2027
Host institution Yale University
Program area Peace and reconciliation
Opportunity type Fellowship
Cohort 2027
Application status Applications open
Application deadline September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT
Application fee US$20
Application method Online
Résumé/CV limit Maximum 3 pages
Personal statement Maximum 600 words
Video statement 90 seconds
Recommendation letters 1
English requirement Fluent English
Nationality requirement Citizens of countries other than the United States
In-person components Yale University, New Haven, USA, and Rose Castle, UK
Travel, lodging and meals Covered for the required in-person components
Program opening April 12–16, 2027, New Haven
Program closing June 14–18, 2027, Rose Castle, UK

What Is the Yale Peace Fellowship?

The Yale Peace Fellowship is an international leadership development opportunity for professionals whose work is connected to peace and reconciliation.

Rather than being designed primarily for students seeking an academic degree, the fellowship is intended for accomplished practitioners who are already doing meaningful work and who want to deepen their leadership abilities, broaden their understanding of peacebuilding, and connect with an international community of people working toward peaceful and constructive solutions to conflict.

The program places particular emphasis on diversity of experience and perspective. Each cohort is geographically balanced and brings together people with different professional backgrounds, talents, experiences, cultures, perspectives, and approaches to peace and reconciliation.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to professionals who can contribute not only through their existing achievements but also through their ability to learn from people whose experiences and approaches differ from their own.

Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 Yale Peace Fellowship is:

September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Yale specifically advises applicants to submit their applications 24 hours before the deadline.

No extensions will be granted.

This is particularly important because applicants must complete several components before their application can be submitted, including the application form, résumé or CV, personal statement, video statement, recommendation request, and application fee.

Applicants can create an account, begin working on their application, save their progress, return later, upload materials, and request their recommendation letter before submitting the completed application.

Who Is Eligible for the Yale Peace Fellowship?

The Yale Peace Fellowship is intended for experienced professionals and practitioners with a demonstrated commitment to peace and reconciliation.

Applicants should meet the following general requirements.

1. Experience in Peace and Reconciliation

Applicants should be accomplished in the field of peace and reconciliation.

This means that competitive applicants should be able to demonstrate meaningful professional work, achievements, leadership, or impact connected to peacebuilding, reconciliation, conflict transformation, social cohesion, dialogue, mediation, or related areas.

The application should make it clear not simply that the applicant is interested in peace, but that they have actually contributed to the field.

2. Demonstrated Leadership

Applicants should have a strong track record of leadership and a clear desire to continue growing professionally.

Leadership does not necessarily have to mean holding the highest formal position within an organization. What matters is evidence that the applicant has taken responsibility, influenced others, initiated or led meaningful work, solved difficult problems, or contributed to measurable change.

Applicants should therefore use their application materials to demonstrate:

  • Leadership responsibilities
  • Professional accomplishments
  • Projects or initiatives they have led
  • Problems they have addressed
  • Communities or organizations they have served
  • Results achieved through their work
  • Evidence of professional growth
  • Future leadership ambitions

3. Commitment to Cross-Cultural Understanding

The fellowship places considerable importance on the ability to engage constructively across cultures and perspectives.

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to cross-cultural understanding and show that they can work respectfully with people who have different experiences, identities, backgrounds, professional disciplines, and worldviews.

This is particularly relevant because the fellowship brings together a geographically diverse cohort.

4. Citizenship Outside the United States

Applicants should be citizens of a country other than the United States.

Applicants who hold dual citizenship with the United States are eligible. However, strong preference is given to candidates whose work is focused outside the United States.

Consequently, the opportunity is fundamentally international in its orientation and is designed to bring together practitioners working in different parts of the world.

5. English Fluency

Applicants must be fluent in English.

English proficiency is important because Fellows are expected to participate fully in the program, communicate with other participants, engage in discussions, and contribute to the program’s activities.

6. Professional Experience

The program typically looks for applicants with a minimum of five years of significant professional experience.

This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for established practitioners rather than individuals who are only beginning their professional careers.

High-level, full-time internships that involved substantial leadership, responsibility, and relevant professional work may count toward the experience requirement, particularly where the internship was closely connected to the objectives of the fellowship.

Which Countries Can Apply?

The Yale Peace Fellowship is an international opportunity.

There is no stated restriction limiting applications to a particular African, Asian, European, North American, South American, Middle Eastern, or Oceanian country.

The principal nationality requirement is that applicants should be citizens of a country other than the United States.

Dual U.S. citizens may apply, although the program gives strong preference to candidates whose professional work is focused outside the United States.

Therefore, qualified applicants from countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions may be considered, provided they satisfy the fellowship’s eligibility and selection requirements.

Is the Yale Peace Fellowship Fully Funded?

The fellowship does not charge Fellows direct participation costs for the program itself.

Importantly, the program states that the costs associated with required in-person components, including travel, lodging, and food, will be covered.

Applicants must, however, pay a US$20 electronic application fee in order to submit their application.

The application fee is mandatory, and Yale states that fee waivers are not available.

What Does the Program Cover?

For the required in-person components, the program covers costs such as:

  • Travel
  • Lodging
  • Food and meals

Applicants should therefore distinguish between the US$20 application fee, which applicants must pay, and the costs of participating in the required in-person portions of the fellowship, which are covered by the program.

Required In-Person Participation

One of the most important requirements is that Fellows must be available to participate fully in all parts of the program.

This includes both virtual and in-person components.

The in-person components cannot be completed online.

For the 2027 cohort, the required in-person gatherings include:

Opening Convening at Yale University

April 12–16, 2027

Location:

Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, United States

This opening convening brings Fellows together at Yale University’s campus at the beginning of the relevant in-person program period.

Closing Convening at Rose Castle

June 14–18, 2027

Location:

Rose Castle, United Kingdom

The closing convening takes place at Rose Castle in the UK.

Applicants who cannot participate in these in-person components should not apply on the assumption that they can complete them remotely. Full participation is a condition of being a Fellow.

What Documents Are Required?

Applicants must complete the application entirely online.

There are no paper forms that applicants need to print, complete, or mail.

The application requires several important materials.

1. Résumé or Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a résumé or CV of no more than three pages.

Because admission is highly competitive, applicants should use the limited space strategically.

A strong résumé should clearly communicate:

  • Professional experience
  • Leadership positions
  • Peace and reconciliation work
  • Major achievements
  • Relevant projects
  • Community or organizational impact
  • International or cross-cultural experience
  • Awards or recognition where relevant
  • Education and professional development

The three-page maximum means applicants should prioritize evidence that directly supports their candidacy.

2. Personal Statement

Applicants must submit a personal statement of no more than 600 words.

This is one of the most important parts of the application because it gives applicants an opportunity to explain their background, motivations, experiences, ambitions, and potential contribution to the fellowship.

The statement should not simply repeat the résumé.

Instead, applicants should use it to communicate the story behind their work and explain why participating in the Yale Peace Fellowship would be meaningful for their professional development and future impact.

3. 90-Second Video Statement

Applicants are required to submit a 90-second video statement, which is recorded directly through the application system.

Applicants receive two attempts to record the video.

The recording stops automatically at the 90-second mark.

If an applicant is dissatisfied with the first recording, they may use their second attempt. However, the second attempt is the final opportunity.

No additional recording attempts are permitted.

Applicants are therefore strongly advised to prepare and practice their response before starting the recording.

4. One Letter of Recommendation

Applicants must submit one letter of recommendation.

Only one recommendation letter is accepted per applicant.

The recommendation letter is confidential and cannot be shared with the applicant.

Applicants should select a recommender who knows their professional work well and can provide credible evidence of their leadership, achievements, character, professional development, and potential.

How to Apply for the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027

The application process is entirely online.

Applicants can begin the process before they are ready to submit their final application, allowing them to work on different sections over time.

The general process is:

Step 1: Create an Application Account

Applicants begin by creating an account on the online application system.

After creating an account, applicants can access the application and begin completing the required sections.

Step 2: Complete the Application Form

Provide the requested personal, professional, and background information accurately.

Applicants should carefully review all information before submission because the application cannot be edited after it has been submitted.

Step 3: Prepare the Résumé or CV

Upload a résumé or CV that does not exceed three pages.

The document should emphasize the professional experiences and achievements most relevant to peace and reconciliation and leadership.

Step 4: Write the Personal Statement

Prepare the required personal statement of no more than 600 words.

The statement should clearly communicate the applicant’s experience, motivation, leadership journey, commitment to peace and reconciliation, and potential contribution to the fellowship.

Step 5: Prepare for the Video Statement

The video statement must be recorded in the application system.

Because there are only two attempts, applicants should prepare their response in advance and practice delivering it within 90 seconds.

Step 6: Request the Recommendation Letter

Enter the details of the selected recommender through the application’s recommendations section.

The recommender will receive instructions for submitting the confidential letter.

Applicants should contact their recommender early enough to ensure the recommendation is submitted on time.

Step 7: Pay the US$20 Application Fee

An electronic application fee of US$20 is required to complete the submission.

The program does not provide application fee waivers.

Another person may pay the fee on behalf of an applicant.

Step 8: Review and Submit

Applicants should carefully review the entire application before submitting it.

Once submitted, the application cannot be edited.

For this reason, applicants should avoid submitting incomplete, outdated, or rushed materials.

Can Someone Else Pay the Application Fee?

Yes.

The Yale Peace Fellowship allows someone else to pay the US$20 application fee on an applicant’s behalf.

The process involves:

  1. Going to the applicant status page.
  2. Selecting the option to submit the US$20 payment.
  3. Opening the payment page.
  4. Copying the payment URL.
  5. Sending the payment URL to the person who will make the payment.

This can be useful for applicants whose application fee is being covered by a family member, organization, employer, colleague, sponsor, or another supporter.

What Happens If the Recommendation Letter Is Late?

The program states that late recommendation letters may still be accepted.

However, applicants should not rely on this flexibility.

The program strongly encourages recommenders to submit their letters by the application deadline. Although efforts will be made to include late letters, the program cannot guarantee that a recommendation submitted after the deadline will be reviewed.

Applicants should therefore request their recommendation well in advance.

Can Applicants Submit More Than One Recommendation?

No.

Only one letter of recommendation is accepted per applicant.

This policy is intended to maintain a consistent and equitable application review process.

Can Applicants See Their Recommendation Letter?

No.

Recommendation letters are confidential and cannot be shared with applicants.

Can Applicants Change Their Recommender?

Yes.

Applicants who need to change their recommender can do so through the Recommendations link at the bottom of their application status page.

Applicants should make any necessary changes in a single session and carefully follow the instructions provided by the application system.

What If the Recommender Has Technical Problems?

If a recommender experiences difficulties uploading their letter, the program provides an alternative route for resolving persistent technical issues.

The recommender may contact the program directly or submit the letter by email as instructed by the program.

Applicants should ensure that the email address associated with the recommendation corresponds with the email address used in their application so that the recommendation can be correctly matched to their file.

What Does “In Progress” Mean for a Recommendation?

If the application system shows a recommendation as “in progress,” this means that the recommender has accessed the submission link but has not yet uploaded the recommendation letter.

Applicants should therefore contact the recommender if the status remains incomplete as the deadline approaches.

Can You Edit the Application After Submission?

No.

Once the Yale Peace Fellowship application has been submitted, applicants cannot make further edits.

Applicants also cannot submit updated or revised materials after the deadline.

If the selection committee needs additional information, the program will contact the applicant directly.

This makes the final review stage particularly important. Applicants should check every section, document, statement, and required component before clicking submit.

Can Applicants Request a Deadline Extension?

No.

The program does not grant deadline extensions.

The official deadline is:

September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit at least 24 hours before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

What Happens If Multiple Applications Are Created?

Applicants should be careful not to create multiple applications under the same account.

The program notes that situations can occur where multiple applications are started under one account. If an applicant receives a message suggesting that an application was not submitted despite having submitted one, the program will review the situation and retain the submitted version while disregarding the duplicate.

Applicants should therefore avoid creating unnecessary duplicate applications.

Technical Problems With the Application

The program does not provide individual technical support for application-system problems.

If an applicant experiences technical difficulties, the recommended approach is to try:

  • A different web browser
  • A different device
  • A different computer
  • A reliable internet connection

Applicants should not leave their application until the last minute because technical problems close to the deadline could make it difficult to submit on time.

Important Video Application Rules

The video statement is particularly important because applicants have only two recording attempts.

Each applicant receives:

  • First recording attempt
  • Second and final recording attempt

The recording automatically stops at 90 seconds.

Applicants cannot request a third attempt simply because they dislike their final recording.

The best approach is to write down the key points of the response, practice speaking naturally, time the response repeatedly, and only begin recording after confirming that the response can be delivered comfortably within the 90-second limit.

How Competitive Is the Yale Peace Fellowship?

Admission is described as highly competitive.

The fellowship does not simply seek applicants with an interest in peace. It seeks accomplished practitioners who can demonstrate leadership, professional achievement, commitment to peace and reconciliation, cross-cultural understanding, and the potential to contribute meaningfully to the cohort.

The geographically balanced nature of the cohort also means that applicants are considered within an international pool containing people with different professional backgrounds and experiences.

Consequently, meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not guarantee admission.

How Can Applicants Strengthen Their Application?

Because the program cannot provide personalized feedback about an individual’s competitiveness, applicants should use their application materials to communicate their strongest evidence of impact and potential.

Demonstrate Impact, Not Just Responsibilities

Instead of simply listing job duties, explain what changed because of your work.

For example, describe:

  • A peacebuilding initiative you created
  • A conflict-resolution process you helped facilitate
  • A community program you led
  • A policy change you contributed to
  • A reconciliation initiative you supported
  • A measurable improvement resulting from your work
  • A difficult challenge you helped resolve

Show Leadership

Leadership should appear throughout the application.

Applicants should demonstrate how they have:

  • Taken initiative
  • Built teams
  • Mobilized communities
  • Influenced institutions
  • Developed solutions
  • Managed complex situations
  • Mentored others
  • Led change

Explain Your Cross-Cultural Experience

Since cross-cultural understanding is central to the fellowship, applicants should explain how they have worked with people from different backgrounds.

This may include professional, community, regional, national, or international experiences.

Make the Personal Statement Personal

The personal statement should reveal something that the résumé cannot.

Applicants should explain why peace and reconciliation matter to them, what experiences shaped their professional direction, what they have learned from their work, and what they hope to accomplish in the future.

Prepare the Video Carefully

The 90-second video is short, so applicants should avoid trying to communicate their entire career history.

A focused response is more effective than attempting to cover too many subjects.

Applicants should aim to communicate their most important message clearly and naturally.

What Costs Does the Fellowship Cover?

According to the program information, there are no direct participation costs associated with the fellowship.

The program covers costs associated with the required in-person components, including:

  • Travel
  • Lodging
  • Food

However, applicants must pay the US$20 application fee to submit their application.

There are no application fee waivers.

Is the Fellowship a Degree Program?

The Yale Peace Fellowship should not be confused with admission to a Yale degree program.

It is a professional fellowship focused on peace and reconciliation and leadership development.

Applicants should therefore apply because they are interested in professional development, international engagement, peacebuilding, reconciliation, and leadership rather than because they are seeking admission to a Yale undergraduate, master’s, doctoral, or other degree program.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Yale Peace Fellowship may be particularly relevant to professionals working in areas such as:

  • Peacebuilding
  • Reconciliation
  • Conflict resolution
  • Mediation
  • Dialogue
  • Community peace initiatives
  • Human rights and peace-related work
  • Social cohesion
  • Conflict transformation
  • International development connected to peace
  • Civil society
  • Public policy related to peace and reconciliation
  • Community leadership
  • Other professional fields directly contributing to peaceful societies

The central consideration is not simply the applicant’s job title. The applicant should be able to demonstrate meaningful accomplishment and leadership in work connected to peace and reconciliation.

Application Checklist

Before submitting the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 application, applicants should confirm that they have completed all of the following:

  • Created an online application account
  • Confirmed their eligibility
  • Confirmed citizenship requirements
  • Confirmed English fluency
  • Confirmed availability for all required program components
  • Prepared a résumé/CV of no more than three pages
  • Written a personal statement of no more than 600 words
  • Prepared for the 90-second video statement
  • Identified one suitable recommender
  • Requested the recommendation letter
  • Checked the recommendation status
  • Prepared the US$20 application fee
  • Reviewed every section of the application
  • Checked all uploaded materials
  • Recorded the video carefully
  • Submitted the application before the deadline

Important Dates for the 2027 Yale Peace Fellowship

Applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

Application deadline: September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT

Recommended submission time: At least 24 hours before the official deadline

Opening convening: April 12–16, 2027, at Yale University in New Haven, United States

Closing convening: June 14–18, 2027, at Rose Castle, United Kingdom

Applicants must be available to participate in the required in-person components. These components cannot be completed virtually.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants should use Yale’s official Peace Fellowship application information and application portal when preparing and submitting their applications.

Applicants should also review Yale University’s relevant equal opportunity and nondiscrimination information before applying.

Apply HERE today!

Frequently Asked Questions About the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027

What is the deadline for the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027?

The deadline is September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit at least 24 hours early.

How much is the application fee?

The application fee is US$20.

Is the application fee refundable or waivable?

The program states that fee waivers cannot be granted. Payment of the fee is required to submit a complete application.

Can someone else pay my application fee?

Yes. Applicants can send the payment-page URL to another person who will pay the US$20 fee on their behalf.

Can I apply if I am a U.S. citizen?

The standard requirement is citizenship in a country other than the United States. Dual U.S. citizens may apply, although strong preference is given to candidates whose work is focused outside the United States.

Do I need five years of professional experience?

The program typically looks for candidates with a minimum of five years of significant professional experience. Relevant high-level, full-time internships involving substantial responsibility and leadership may count in some circumstances.

Do I need to attend the in-person sessions?

Yes. Full participation in all components of the program is required.

Can the in-person sessions be attended online?

No. The in-person components cannot be completed online.

How many recommendation letters are required?

Only one recommendation letter is required and accepted.

Can I submit more than one recommendation?

No. The program accepts only one recommendation letter per applicant.

How long can my CV be?

The résumé or CV must be a maximum of three pages.

How long can the personal statement be?

The personal statement must be a maximum of 600 words.

How long is the video statement?

The video statement is 90 seconds.

How many video attempts do I get?

Each applicant receives two attempts. The second attempt is final.

Can I edit my application after submitting it?

No. Once submitted, the application cannot be edited.

Can I submit updated materials after the deadline?

No. Revised or additional materials cannot be submitted after the deadline unless the selection committee specifically contacts the applicant for further information.

Are deadline extensions available?

No. The program does not grant extensions.

Are travel and accommodation covered?

Yes. Costs associated with the required in-person components, including travel, lodging, and food, are covered by the program.

To learn more about the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027, click HERE.

Final Advice for Applicants

The Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 represents an opportunity for experienced peace and reconciliation practitioners to join an international cohort and develop their leadership capabilities in a highly competitive environment.

Applicants should not approach the application as a simple eligibility exercise. Meeting the minimum requirements is only the starting point. A strong application should demonstrate a clear record of accomplishment, meaningful leadership, commitment to peace and reconciliation, the ability to engage across cultures, and a compelling vision for future impact.

The most important materials should work together. The résumé should establish the applicant’s professional record, the personal statement should explain the motivations and experiences behind that record, the recommendation should provide an independent perspective on the applicant’s abilities and potential, and the video should communicate the applicant’s personality and message clearly within the strict 90-second limit.

Applicants should also take the logistical requirements seriously. The September 9, 2026, at 14:00 EDT deadline is firm, the US$20 application fee is mandatory, and the required in-person components cannot be completed remotely.

Most importantly, prospective applicants should begin early. Preparing a thoughtful personal statement, selecting the right recommender, practicing the video response, reviewing the application carefully, and resolving technical or payment issues before the final day can help prevent avoidable problems.

For professionals who have already made meaningful contributions to peace and reconciliation and are ready to expand their leadership, networks, and international perspective, the Yale Peace Fellowship 2027 offers a significant opportunity to learn alongside practitioners from different parts of the world and further develop their capacity to contribute to peace.

To explore and learn more about other fellowship opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Maps Learning Hub offers free, self-paced online training for people interested in Geographic Information Systems, OpenStreetMap, QGIS, digital mapping and open geospatial information.

Developed through the UN Maps initiative and provided by the United Nations Global Service Centre, the platform gives learners an opportunity to develop practical mapping skills that can support development, peacekeeping, sustainability, humanitarian action and emergency-response activities.

The learning platform is open to participants from around the world, regardless of nationality or professional background. Most courses are publicly accessible after creating an account, although selected courses concerning internal United Nations systems are restricted to UN personnel.

There is currently no application deadline. Learners can register, enrol and begin studying through the UN Maps Learning Hub at their own pace.

What Is the UN Maps Learning Hub?

The UN Maps Learning Hub is an online self-training platform that teaches learners how to understand, create, edit, analyse and use open geospatial information.

The platform is closely connected with UN Mappers, a global community of volunteers and geospatial contributors who improve open geographic data in support of United Nations activities.

Its educational content covers several areas, including:

  • OpenStreetMap fundamentals
  • Basic and advanced geographic data editing
  • Mapping geographic features and objects
  • OpenStreetMap data validation
  • Land-use and land-cover mapping
  • QGIS analysis
  • Digital map creation
  • UN Maps applications and tools
  • UN Geoportal functions for authorized personnel
  • The use of open geospatial information in development and peacekeeping contexts

The platform is designed for different levels of experience. A complete beginner can start with introductory OpenStreetMap lessons, while a more experienced mapper can move to advanced editing, validation, QGIS analysis and map-production topics.

According to the official UN Maps learning page, the Learning Hub is intended to provide an all-in-one educational pathway for people who want to build geospatial skills and contribute more effectively to UN Maps initiatives.

Is the UN Maps Learning Hub Free?

Access to the UN Maps Learning Hub is free.

The official platform does not publish tuition fees, application charges or subscription costs. Learners are required to create an account to enrol in courses and track their progress.

The learning materials relating to OpenStreetMap are also released under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 licence, commonly known as CC BY-SA 2.0. This supports the reuse and adaptation of the materials, subject to the applicable attribution and share-alike conditions.

Application Deadline

There is no published application or enrolment deadline for the self-paced courses.

The platform operates as an ongoing online learning resource. Participants can generally create an account, select an available course and begin studying without waiting for a fixed annual application cycle.

Because course availability may change, learners should review the official portal before enrolling.

Courses Available on the UN Maps Learning Hub

The public course catalogue currently identifies four major learning areas.

1. OpenStreetMap Basics

The OpenStreetMap Basics course is the recommended starting point for learners who have little or no previous mapping experience.

OpenStreetMap is a collaborative global project that creates and maintains a free, editable map of the world. Contributors add and improve information about roads, buildings, waterways, land use, public facilities and other geographic features.

The introductory course is designed to help learners understand:

  • What OpenStreetMap is
  • How collaborative open mapping works
  • How geographic information is represented
  • How to begin editing OpenStreetMap
  • How to use the principal OpenStreetMap editing tools
  • How to identify and map common geographic objects
  • How to follow appropriate mapping practices
  • How geographic data can support UN-related activities
  • How individual contributors can participate in the wider mapping community

The platform explains that its courses include geographic objects encountered in areas associated with United Nations peacekeeping missions supported by the UN Maps initiative.

Beginners are advised to complete the introductory learning material before moving to advanced editing and validation.

2. OpenStreetMap Advanced

The OpenStreetMap Advanced course is intended for learners who already understand basic OpenStreetMap concepts and editing practices.

The advanced learning path builds deeper technical capabilities in areas such as:

  • Advanced OpenStreetMap editing
  • Geographic data quality
  • Data validation
  • Identification and correction of mapping errors
  • Complex mapping situations
  • Land-use and land-cover mapping
  • Interpretation of available imagery
  • Consistency and completeness of mapped features
  • Advanced contribution workflows

Data validation is particularly important in collaborative mapping. Open geographic databases receive contributions from users with varying levels of experience, so advanced contributors help review information, identify inconsistencies and improve overall data quality.

The UN Maps learning pathway specifically connects its advanced OpenStreetMap track with validation and land-cover mapping.

3. QGIS Training

QGIS is a widely used open-source Geographic Information System application. It allows users to view, manage, analyse, combine and present geospatial data.

The QGIS training component expands the Learning Hub beyond basic map editing. It is intended to help participants understand how geographic information can be analysed and converted into useful maps or other visual products.

Depending on the available course modules, QGIS-related learning may support the development of skills associated with:

  • Understanding GIS concepts
  • Working with geographic datasets
  • Managing spatial layers
  • Displaying and styling geographic information
  • Conducting geospatial analysis
  • Creating maps
  • Presenting spatial results
  • Using open-source GIS tools for practical assignments
  • Supporting evidence-based planning and decision-making

QGIS can be useful to students and professionals working in urban planning, environmental management, disaster-risk reduction, infrastructure, public administration, development, humanitarian assistance and academic research.

The QGIS course was introduced on the Learning Hub during 2025. UN Maps reported that the platform had hosted 3,111 learners by the end of that year. UN Mappers 2025 review

4. UN Geoportal Basics

The UN Geoportal Basics course concerns the use of the United Nations Geoportal and is marked as available to UN staff only.

This restriction exists because the course deals with systems or functions that may not be accessible to the general public.

Eligible UN personnel may use this course to build knowledge of relevant Geoportal tools and workflows. Members of the public should not assume that registration on the Learning Hub will automatically grant them access to restricted United Nations applications.

The UN Maps Learning Path

The broader UN Maps Learning Path organizes educational content around different audiences and technical needs.

UN Track

The UN Track begins with very basic OpenStreetMap editing. Its purpose is to help authorized users understand how basemap information can be updated through UN Maps tools.

The track then provides more detailed guidance on the features and functions of UN Maps applications through instructional material, videos and walkthroughs.

Some parts of this track may be limited to United Nations personnel because they involve tools that are not publicly accessible.

OpenStreetMap Track

The OpenStreetMap Track is designed for both new and experienced UN Mappers.

The track may include:

  • Basic OpenStreetMap learning for beginners
  • More advanced mapping practices
  • Data-validation techniques
  • Land-use and land-cover mapping
  • Progressive development of open-mapping capabilities

Learners can begin at the level most appropriate to their existing skills.

UN OpenGIS Track

The UN OpenGIS learning track is intended to provide educational resources concerning open-source GIS software through collaboration with the UN-GGIM Academic Network.

The official learning-path page identifies this track as not yet released. Prospective learners should therefore verify its current status on the portal rather than assuming that all planned material is already available.

Self-Paced and Independent Learning

The courses are structured for online self-training.

This means participants do not ordinarily need to attend classes at a fixed physical location. Learners can work through the available content using an internet-connected computer or compatible device.

The courses are independent and can be accessed in different orders. However, beginners are encouraged to follow the suggested sequence, starting with basic OpenStreetMap learning before moving to more advanced content.

The platform allows registered users to:

  • Enrol in available courses
  • Access online learning materials
  • Track learning progress
  • Complete quizzes
  • Take tests covering individual sections
  • Attempt assessments for an entire course
  • Develop skills progressively
  • Receive available participation badges

The exact length of study will depend on the selected course, the learner’s existing knowledge and the amount of time dedicated to practical exercises.

Languages Supported

The UN Maps Learning Hub is multilingual.

The broader UN Maps learning page states that educational content is supported in the six official languages of the United Nations:

  • Arabic
  • Chinese
  • English
  • French
  • Russian
  • Spanish

Additional languages may become available through community-led translation initiatives.

Not every individual course or module should automatically be assumed to be fully available in every supported language. Learners should check the selected course after logging in to confirm the languages currently offered for that content.

Do the Courses Provide Certificates?

Learners should distinguish between participation badges, course-completion recognition and the planned UN Mappers certification system.

The UN Maps Learning Hub states that registered participants can complete quizzes and tests and may receive badges of participation.

However, the public landing page describes the comprehensive UN Mappers certificate as a future feature. The proposed certification process is expected to involve:

  1. Passing an evaluation covering knowledge taught through the Learning Hub.
  2. Completing several UN Mappers project tasks in different mapping contexts.
  3. Submitting the completed work for review by the UN Mappers team.
  4. Responding to feedback and making corrections or improvements where required.

Therefore, applicants should not promote the current self-paced courses as automatically providing a formal United Nations professional certificate unless the specific course page expressly confirms that one is available.

A participation badge is not necessarily equivalent to an accredited academic qualification, professional licence or formal UN employment credential.

Who Can Join the UN Maps Learning Hub?

The public learning platform is accessible to people around the world who want to learn about open geospatial information.

Potential learners include:

  • University and college students
  • Recent graduates
  • Teachers and academic researchers
  • GIS professionals
  • Urban and regional planners
  • Surveying and geography students
  • Environmental professionals
  • Humanitarian workers
  • Development practitioners
  • Disaster-management professionals
  • Public-sector employees
  • Data analysts
  • Civil-society organizations
  • Open-source technology enthusiasts
  • OpenStreetMap contributors
  • Volunteers interested in UN Mappers
  • People with no previous mapping experience

No university degree, professional certification or previous employment experience is listed as a general requirement for the publicly available courses.

Some technical modules may be easier for learners with previous GIS or mapping knowledge, but beginners can start with the OpenStreetMap Basics course.

How the Learning Can Support United Nations Activities

Open geospatial information can help organizations understand where communities, infrastructure, natural features and services are located.

High-quality maps can support activities related to:

  • Peacekeeping operations
  • Sustainable development
  • Humanitarian response
  • Disaster preparedness
  • Emergency relief
  • Infrastructure planning
  • Environmental assessment
  • Community development
  • Agricultural planning
  • Public-service delivery
  • Accessibility analysis
  • Field logistics
  • Evidence-based decision-making

UN Mappers contributors have supported projects involving peacekeeping missions and other UN entities. UN Maps reported that volunteer mapping contributed to mapsheets supporting the United Nations Support Office in Somalia and the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic.

The initiative also supported the Food and Agriculture Organization by producing baseline map data for agricultural planning along the Senegal River in Mauritania.

The UN Mappers Community

The Learning Hub is connected with the wider UN Mappers community.

According to the UN Maps community page, the initiative includes more than 6,000 volunteers worldwide and has conducted more than 400 mapping events and capacity-building activities since 2020.

Community members may participate in:

  • Collaborative mapping projects
  • Online or in-person training
  • Mapathons
  • Mapping parties
  • Technical discussions
  • Emergency mapping activities
  • Community events
  • Knowledge-sharing sessions
  • Mapping challenges
  • Volunteer contributions supporting UN operations

Learners who complete the courses can use their new skills to explore these collaborative opportunities. Course registration itself, however, should not be interpreted as employment, an internship or formal appointment with the United Nations.

Community Support for Learners

The UN Mappers community provides support for newcomers who encounter technical or learning-related questions.

Learners may seek help through:

  • UN Mappers communication channels
  • Social media
  • The UN Mappers Discord community
  • Email support
  • Experienced geospatial contributors

For customer support, learners can contact:

Email: un.mappers@un.org

For feedback and suggestions concerning UN Maps, users can contact:

Email: maps@un.org

How to Register and Start Learning

Prospective learners can follow these steps:

  1. Visit the UN Maps Learning Hub.
  2. Select the option to log in or create a new account.
  3. Complete the required account-registration process.
  4. Confirm the account if email verification is requested.
  5. Log in to the platform.
  6. Review the available course catalogue.
  7. Select a suitable learning pathway.
  8. Enrol in the chosen course.
  9. Begin with introductory material if you are new to mapping.
  10. Complete the lessons, practical activities, quizzes and tests.
  11. Monitor progress through the learner account.
  12. Claim any participation badge made available after meeting the relevant requirements.

The login page also displays supported institutional or third-party sign-in options, including Azure and LinkedIn. Available login methods may change, so users should follow the options shown on the official registration page.

Recommended Learning Order for Beginners

Although courses can be taken independently, a new learner may benefit from the following sequence:

  1. OpenStreetMap Basics
  2. Practical OpenStreetMap editing
  3. OpenStreetMap Advanced
  4. Data validation
  5. Land-use and land-cover mapping
  6. QGIS Training
  7. UN Maps or UN Geoportal material, where eligible

This progression allows the learner to begin with basic geographic concepts and gradually advance toward data validation, analysis and professional map production.

Important Points to Remember

Before registering, prospective learners should understand that:

  • The Learning Hub is an educational platform, not a recruitment portal.
  • Registration does not create an employment relationship with the United Nations.
  • Most public courses are free and self-paced.
  • Some courses are restricted to UN personnel.
  • There is no published general enrolment deadline.
  • An account is required to track progress.
  • Learners may complete quizzes and tests.
  • Participation badges may be available.
  • A comprehensive UN Mappers certificate is described as a future feature and should not be assumed to be currently available.
  • Course availability, languages and recognition may vary.
  • Formal educational or professional qualifications are not generally required for public courses.

Why the UN Maps Learning Hub Is Valuable

The Learning Hub combines several valuable features within one platform:

  • Free access to geospatial learning
  • Beginner and advanced course options
  • Training in OpenStreetMap and QGIS
  • Practical connection to global development work
  • Multilingual educational resources
  • Self-paced online study
  • Knowledge tests and progress tracking
  • Access to a worldwide mapping community
  • Opportunities to contribute to open geographic data
  • Exposure to the role of mapping in peacekeeping and humanitarian work

For students and early-career professionals, the platform can provide an accessible introduction to geospatial information. For experienced mappers, it can offer advanced learning in validation, land-cover mapping and the application of open geographic data.

Conclusion

The UN Maps Learning Hub provides a free and globally accessible pathway for learning OpenStreetMap, QGIS, geospatial analysis and digital map creation.

Participants can begin with basic OpenStreetMap concepts, progress to advanced editing and data validation, and develop GIS analysis and map-making skills through QGIS training. The platform supports multiple languages, provides quizzes and progress tracking, and connects learners with the wider UN Mappers community.

There is no published general application deadline, and most public courses do not require a degree, professional experience or previous GIS knowledge. However, some courses involving internal United Nations systems are reserved for UN personnel.

Anyone interested in geographic data, humanitarian mapping, sustainable development, public planning, emergency response or open-source GIS can visit the official platform, create an account and begin learning.
